patient.history_present_illness: Mr. Garcia is a 19-year-old college freshman with no medical history who is brought by EMS from a college party where he was found convulsing continuously for approximately 15 minutes. His friends report he ingested an unknown pill approximately 60-90 minutes before the seizure onset — they believe it may have been sold as 'Molly' (MDMA) but acknowledge they are not certain what it was. He had also consumed approximately 4-5 alcoholic drinks during the evening. He has absolutely no prior history of seizures. He has no medical conditions and takes no medications. On EMS arrival he was in continuous generalized tonic-clonic activity with severe agitation and hyperthermia. Temperature on EMS arrival was 39.6°C.

output.summary: Rhabdomyolysis with AKI: aggressive IV isotonic saline targeting urine output 1–3 mL/kg/h. Urine alkalinisation with sodium bicarbonate may reduce myoglobin precipitation in renal tubules. Active cooling for hyperthermia limits ongoing muscle damage. Monitoring of potassium, cardiac rhythm, and creatinine is required; nephrology consultation is recommended when AKI is evolving.

output.summary: Tricyclic antidepressant toxicity causes seizures via GABA-A antagonism and CNS sodium channel blockade. QRS above 100 ms indicates significant sodium channel blockade; sodium bicarbonate (1–2 mEq/kg IV) is the treatment — alkalemia increases TCA protein binding and the sodium load overcomes channel blockade. Terminal R wave in aVR above 3 mm and QRS above 100 ms are specific indicators of TCA toxicity. Phenytoin is contraindicated for TCA-induced SE as it worsens sodium channel blockade and increases cardiac toxicity. Benzodiazepines, levetiracetam, and phenobarbital are used for seizure management.
